correctness.rationale: The displayed spectral theorem and Cesàro inequality are correct. The gap of a pair k<l is 4|sin((l-k)a) sin((l+k)a+θ)|. If n is odd, the lower bound uses sin a and the smaller of sin θ and sin(a-θ); pairs ((n-1)/2,(n+1)/2) and (0,n-1) attain the respective branches. If n is even, sum and difference have the same parity modulo n. Even sums give sin θ and nonzero even differences give sin(2a), attained at (1,n-1); odd sums give sin(a-θ) and odd differences give sin a, attained at (0,n-1). These witnesses include n=3,4 and give zero at the appropriate endpoints. One branch increases and the other decreases, so their unique crossing gives π/2 or n arctan(tan(a)/3); the optimal values and limits follow by substitution and small-angle expansions. The n(n-1) off-diagonal position terms each carry magnitude 1/n² and integrate to at most 2/(Tg_n) after time averaging, yielding the displayed inequality. Line 55 reverses the direction in prose: the optimizer maximizes the denominator g_n and minimizes the right-hand side, not the denominator itself. It need not optimize actual mixing. Independent direct all-pair comparisons at 48 size–flux points agreed within 1.33e-15 and all eight explicit optimum values agreed.
residual_risks: The replay is bounded. The inequality's optimization is not an optimization of actual finite-time mixing. The wording slip noted above is not used in the proof.
